The **Soybean_Cyst_Nematode** reference (bottom-right panel) is a striking match — it shows soybean plants with bright yellow margins and green centers across a canopy, nearly identical to the test image.

Key visual analysis of the test image:
- **Bright yellow/lime-green margins** on soybean leaves, with **green centers and visible veins retained**
- Affects the **upper canopy uniformly** across multiple plants
- **No discrete spots, lesions, brown necrosis, or fungal structures** visible
- Plants are **still alive and upright** — no wilting or collapse

This marginal chlorosis pattern without brown necrosis distinguishes it from Sudden Death Syndrome (which progresses to interveinal brown necrosis) and Brown Stem Rot (similar pattern but different progression). SCN root feeding causes nutrient stress, producing exactly this bright marginal/interveinal chlorosis pattern visible at the canopy level. The SCN reference collage (bottom-right panel) matches the field appearance almost perfectly.
